title: The Cat and the Birds
summary: Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that the wise are not deceived by an enemy who dresses as a physician.
full_text: Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. A cat dressed as a doctor visited sick birds in an aviary. The surrounding valley lay quiet in the midday heat, yet within the peaceful scene, natural instincts and rival interests were quietly at work. Before long, the initial quiet gave way to a sharp challenge as unexpected circumstances forced both sides to act. The birds replied from high perches: "We will all be perfectly healthy if you will only depart!".... Natural instincts and sharp wits collided, bringing the trial to an immediate, decisive climax. Each party sought to press their advantage, weighing spoken words against unspoken motives. When the decisive moment arrived, neither boastful pretense nor hasty excuses could alter the outcome. The outcome revealed the enduring truth of human character. The experience left behind a timeless truth for all who heard the tale, demonstrating that the wise are not deceived by an enemy who dresses as a physician.
moral: The wise are not deceived by an enemy who dresses as a physician.

quiz.question: What essential truth does "The Cat and the Birds" teach young readers?
options: The wise are not deceived by an enemy who dresses as a physician.
Might and physical strength always triumph over truth and wisdom
Flattery is the safest and most honest way to make lifelong friends
It is wise to pretend to be someone you are not in times of trouble
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the final moral lesson of the fable.
